questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-05 labor data releases (July ADP National Employment Report and July ISM Services PMI) reshape sector risks ahead of Friday Aug 7 BLS payrolls (consensus +80k Reuters / +83k Dow Jones / +90k First Trust): (1) July ADP private payrolls slowed sharply to +44k (vs +75k est, June revised +95k), with ONLY three private sectors shedding jobs: Leisure and hospitality (-11k, worst), Trade, transportation, and utilities (-8k, second worst), and Natural resources/mining (-6k), while Financial activities (+10k), Professional and business services (+9k), Other services (+6k), Information (+5k), Manufacturing (+2k), Construction (+1k), and Education/health (+36k) all posted gains. (2) Simultaneously, July ISM Services PMI edged up to 54.1, but the ISM Services Employment sub-index plunged back into contraction at 47.4 (down from 51.2), citing hiring caution and AI-linked reductions, while explicitly listing retail trade, information, construction, public administration, utilities, mining, and finance & insurance among expanding industries. (3) Leisure and hospitality rises cleanly to #1 (0.21 -> 0.27) on convergent ADP (-11k), RBC post-World Cup drag, KPMG Haitian TPS expirations, and high monthly variance (June -54.6k), tempered by Continuum Economics' rebound call and modest ADP-BLS monthly correlation. (4) Trade, transportation, and utilities jumps to #2 (0.14 -> 0.20) on ADP (-8k), tariff/Middle East supply-chain caution, and its massive ~29M headcount base. (5) Government holds #3 (0.15) as ADP excludes public payrolls and July state/local education seasonal adjustments create large variance on a ~23.5M base. (6) Financial activities drops sharply (0.18 -> 0.10) after ADP +10k and ISM Finance expansion (retaining 0.10 for RBC real-estate/mortgage drag and ADP-BLS divergence). (7) Professional and business services enters #5 at 0.08 (replacing Information, which drops to ~0.05 in residual after ADP +5k, ISM Information expansion, and its small ~3M base) given PBS's huge ~22.8M base and sensitivity to white-collar/AI hiring pullbacks flagged by ISM Employment 47.4. Top-5 sum 0.80 leaves 20% residual across Manufacturing (~0.06, ADP +2k and ISM Mfg Emp 52.8 vs July auto retooling), Information (~0.05), Construction (~0.04), Mining and logging (~0.03, ADP -6k but tiny 0.63M base), Other services (~0.015), and Private education and health services (~0.005).

questions.title: Which districts will hold polling on August 10 in Pakistan-administered Kashmir's 2026 Legislative Assembly election?
questions.background: Pakistan-administered Kashmir's 2026 Legislative Assembly election is scheduled to take place in three phases.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official election-authority records or reliable contemporaneous reporting identifying the districts where polling takes place on August 10, 2026. Resolution : The answer will be the complete set of districts within Pakistan-administered Kashmir where Legislative Assembly polling opens on that date. Accepted Answer Format : The district names, joined by “and”.
questions.current_reasoning: Critical 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-04 updates require a major de-overconfidence repricing from 0.85: (1) Two landslide-delayed Muzaffarabad Phase 2 seats voted today Aug 4 (Hindustan Times/Independent Pakistan), confirming zero spillover from Muzaffarabad/Mirpur into Aug 10. (2) Crucially, Chief Election Commissioner Ghulam Mustafa Mughal explicitly told Independent Pakistan (Aug 3) that for Aug 10 Phase 3 the EC intended to proceed in Bagh (3 seats), Haveli (1 seat), and Abbaspur (1 seat in Poonch district), with both Sudhnoti seats (Baloch & Palandri) 'still under review depending on the security picture' and voting 'not currently planned in Rawalakot city or Thorar' (Poonch), with a final call depending on law-and-order closer to the date. (3) Conversely, AJK EC also fixed Aug 10 for LA-24 Baloch (Sudhnoti) on Aug 3 (Daily Parliament Times) and on Aug 4 categorically denied social-media rumors of postponements in Poonch and Sudhnoti (UrduPoint/Kashmir English/24Urdu), insisting all Poonch Division constituencies remain scheduled for Aug 10 while noting EC will inform the public if any schedule changes occur; meanwhile JKDP formally petitioned CEC on Aug 4 to postpone Poonch Division polls amid deadly Rawalakot clashes. Because Abbaspur is in Poonch district, Poonch still counts even if Rawalakot/Thorar are postponed, keeping all 4 districts ('Poonch, Bagh, Haveli, and Sudhnoti') the clear favorite at 0.58, but sharply lifting partial-postponement slates directly implied by Mughal's remarks: 'Poonch, Bagh, and Haveli' (0.03 -> 0.16, if Sudhnoti's 2 under-review seats are postponed while Abbaspur proceeds), 'Bagh and Haveli' (0.03 -> 0.14, if both Poonch and Sudhnoti hotspots are postponed), 'Bagh, Haveli, and Sudhnoti' (0.05 -> 0.09, if all of Poonch is pulled while Sudhnoti proceeds), and 'Poonch, Bagh, and Sudhnoti' (0.01). Sum 0.98.

questions.title: Which city will be the site of Typhoon Dolphin's first landfall in mainland China in August 2026?
questions.background: Dolphin developed into a typhoon over the Pacific in late July 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Landfall information issued by China's meteorological authorities, either directly or through contemporaneous reliable news coverage. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the city identified as the location of Dolphin's first mainland China landfall during August 2026. Offshore island landfalls do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the city name, rather than its province or a broader geographical region.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-05 official CMA update (18:00 Typhoon Blue Warning via China Daily/CCTV and 21:34 CMA expert briefing via CCTV/CE.cn): At 17:00 Aug 5, Severe Typhoon Dolphin (14 grade, 42 m/s, 955 hPa after eyewall replacement) stood at 25.8N, 136.9E (920 km east of Naha), tracking west at 20-25 km/h (only +0.5N over 5.0W since Aug 4 14:00). Crucially, CMA's Aug 5 21:34 forecast consolidated off yesterday's co-equal Shandong/Jiangsu northern recurvature branch onto a single primary landfall corridor: 'landing along the coast of Zhejiang to northern Fujian on the night of Aug 9 to morning of Aug 10 (Typhoon or Severe Typhoon strength), moving west inland before gradually curving north.' CMA experts still cautioned that mid-latitude westerly trough interaction with the subtropical and South Asian highs leaves substantial uncertainty until Aug 6 (and Shanghai MSA activated Level-4 emergency response at 08:00 Aug 5; Typhoon Whale is also active nearby). Accordingly, re-centering probability mass onto the four mainland prefecture-level cities spanning Zhejiang to northern Fujian (excluding offshore island prefecture Zhoushan per resolution rules): Wenzhou climbs to #1 (0.15 -> 0.22, 27.2N-28.3N dead center of trajectory and corridor), Taizhou rises to #2 (0.17 -> 0.21, 28.1N-29.1N central Zhejiang), Ningde rebounds sharply to #3 (0.10 -> 0.16, 26.4N-27.3N covering all of northern Fujian), Ningbo trims slightly (0.15 -> 0.14, northern Zhejiang + mainland follow-through from Zhoushan), and Shanghai drops (0.13 -> 0.08, absorbing northern-edge/early-trough risk). Top-5 sum 0.81 leaves 19% residual for Fuzhou (~0.07, just south of Ningde), Jiangsu/Nantong/Yancheng (~0.04), Shandong (~0.03), Jiaxing (~0.03), and southern Fujian/other (~0.02).

questions.title: Which club will sign Manor Solomon from Tottenham Hotspur during the summer 2026 transfer window?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the clubs involved or reliable contemporaneous news reporting confirming Solomon's completed transfer from Tottenham Hotspur during the summer 2026 transfer window. Resolution : Resolve when the receiving club confirms the signing or the completed transfer is reliably reported. Transfer rumours and ongoing negotiations do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club signing Solomon.
questions.current_reasoning: Meaningful 2026-08-05 transfer updates from hammers.news (10:31 UK, citing Israeli outlet Sport5) and BBC Sport Gossip strengthen West Ham's lead while cooling Hull City's links: (1) Solomon's agent Shlomi Ben Ezra told Sport5 that a permanent exit should happen 'in the coming days,' that Solomon 'will play in England in the coming year, most likely,' and explicitly praised West Ham as 'a huge club' citing fellow Israelis Yossi Benayoun and Eyal Berkovic, with Solomon now reported as West Ham's priority Crysencio Summerville replacement. (2) While BBC Sport Gossip (Aug 5, citing The i Paper) still noted Hull City interest, Hull owner Acun Ilicali's latest public nationality-flag transfer tracker omitted any Israeli flag, reducing Hull's likelihood of closing a deal. Lifting West Ham United (0.47 -> 0.54, staying strictly below the 0.55 cap for unconfirmed deals since no £10-20m fee is agreed yet and West Ham are in the Championship), trimming Hull City (0.15 -> 0.11) and Fiorentina (0.06 -> 0.04, given 'England most likely' and Mastantuono loan), holding Leeds United (0.04), and nudging Crystal Palace (0.03 -> 0.04) as an English PL fallback. Top-5 sum 0.77 leaves 23% residual for any late Premier League/Championship hijack or European buyer if West Ham-Spurs fee talks stall.

questions.title: From which UK city will the aid boat Kate depart on its Gaza mission in August 2026?
questions.background: The Freedom Flotilla organizes sea voyages aimed at delivering aid to Gaza and challenging Israel's blockade.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the UK city from which Kate sets sail in August 2026 as part of a Freedom Flotilla effort to reach Gaza, according to contemporaneous reporting of its departure. Resolution Date : 2026-08-16 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the city name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Israel's May 19, 2026 interception of the ~60-vessel Global Sumud and Freedom Flotilla Coalition ships from Turkey and Greece (which included 16 UK participants), no public details on the UK aid boat 'Kate' or its August departure port have surfaced as of June 24, 2026. Combining maritime departure logistics toward the Bay of Biscay and Mediterranean with UK pro-Palestine activist hubs and prior Freedom Flotilla host ports (such as Handala's UK stops), Plymouth, Bristol, London, Southampton, and Brighton are the highest-probability UK cities. Because roughly 15-20 UK port cities (including Portsmouth, Liverpool, Cardiff, Glasgow, Belfast, Edinburgh, and Swansea) are genuinely plausible before an announcement, 52% probability mass is left outside the top five to maintain strict calibration.
